projects.name: Analytics Dashboard
projects.description:
End-to-end analytics dashboard project covering three data domains: (1) ingestion and processing of customer CSV files, (2) analysis of application log data, and (3) interactive visualization components. Delivers a unified dashboard for business and engineering stakeholders, with a foundation layer for shared infrastructure, plus integration, testing, and deployment milestones.

Tags: analytics, dashboard, data-pipeline, csv, log-analysis, visualization

tasks.name: M1 — Foundation & Architecture
tasks.details: Milestone roll-up: establish the technical backbone for the dashboard before domain work begins. Covers repo/tooling setup, architecture and data model decisions, and the shared data storage layer. All work is decomposed into subtasks below; this milestone should be tracked by its children.

tasks.name: M2 — Customer CSV Data Processing
tasks.details: Milestone roll-up: ingest, validate, normalize, and model customer CSV data into analytics-ready tables. Includes schema discovery, parsing/validation, cleaning, and enrichment of customer records. Decomposed into subtasks; tracked by its children.

tasks.name: M3 — Application Log Analysis
tasks.details: Milestone roll-up: parse application logs into a structured event model, extract reliability and usage metrics, and derive aggregates for dashboard consumption. Decomposed into subtasks; tracked by its children.

tasks.name: M4 — Visualization Components & Dashboard UI
tasks.details: Milestone roll-up: build the dashboard UI shell and the reusable visualization components that consume customer and log analytics. Covers design system, chart components, dashboard layout, and interactivity. Decomposed into subtasks; tracked by its children.

tasks.name: M5 — Integration, Testing & Deployment
tasks.details: Milestone roll-up: wire the pipelines and UI together end-to-end, verify correctness and performance, and ship to a runnable environment. Decomposed into subtasks; tracked by its children.

tasks.name: Repo scaffold & tooling baseline
tasks.details: Initialize the monorepo/repo layout (e.g., /pipelines, /api, /ui, /infra), add package manifest, linters/formatters, pre-commit hooks, .env.example, and a CI stub that runs lint + tests. Done when a fresh clone can run the lint and test scripts with zero setup surprises.

tasks.name: Architecture decision record & data flow design
tasks.details: Choose stack and processing model (batch vs. micro-batch vs. streaming), sketch the end-to-end data flow (CSV + logs → raw → curated → API → UI), and record decisions as 2–3 short ADRs. Done when an engineer new to the project can follow the diagram and rationale.

tasks.name: Design shared data model & schemas
tasks.details: Define canonical schemas for the customer entity, log event entity, and derived metric tables (field names, types, nullability, primary keys, timestamps in UTC). Publish as schema files (SQL DDL or JSON Schema). Done when downstream CSV, log, and UI tasks can reference a single agreed contract.

tasks.name: Provision storage layer (raw & curated zones)
tasks.details: Set up the local/dev database or warehouse (e.g., DuckDB/Postgres) with raw, staging, and curated schemas plus migration tooling. Done when migrations run cleanly from scratch and a smoke-test table can be written and read.

tasks.name: Data quality standards & PII handling policy
tasks.details: Write a one-page standard covering naming conventions, freshness/quality expectations, and handling of customer PII (masking, allowed fields, retention). Done when the CSV and log tasks have explicit rules for what may be stored and surfaced in the dashboard.

tasks.name: Inventory customer CSV files & formats
tasks.details: Collect a representative sample of customer CSV exports and document delimiters, encodings, header variations, date formats, and known dirty-data patterns. Output a short findings note with 3–5 sample fixtures checked into the repo (anonymized).

tasks.name: Define CSV schema contract & validation rules
tasks.details: Map source CSV columns to the canonical customer schema and specify validation rules (required fields, types, allowed values, duplicate policy, max row-size expectations). Done when every rule is machine-readable and testable by the parser task.

tasks.name: Build CSV parser & raw loader
tasks.details: Implement a chunked CSV reader that detects delimiter/encoding, handles quoted fields and ragged rows, and lands rows in the raw zone with lineage (file name, row number, load timestamp). Done when it ingests a 100k-row sample without memory blow-up and row counts reconcile to the source file.

tasks.name: Implement validation, quarantine & error reporting
tasks.details: Apply the validation rules during load: route failing rows to a quarantine table with a reason code, and emit a per-run summary (rows read / accepted / rejected, top failure reasons). Done when a deliberately corrupted fixture produces a readable rejection report and no bad rows reach staging.

tasks.name: Clean & normalize customer records
tasks.details: Standardize types and formats on staged rows: trim/case-normalize names and emails, parse dates to UTC, normalize country/region codes, handle nulls and duplicates per policy. Done when normalization rules are encoded as a reusable transformation module with unit tests.

tasks.name: Customer identity resolution & enrichment
tasks.details: Assign a canonical customer ID across files, merge duplicate records using deterministic match keys (email, external ID), and attach derived attributes (first/last seen, source file, status). Done when duplicate rates before/after are reported and each customer resolves to exactly one canonical row.

tasks.name: Build curated customer analytics tables
tasks.details: Materialize analytics-ready customer tables: customer dimension, acquisition/cohort attributes, and segment rollups the dashboard will query. Done when each table has documented grain, row count expectations, and freshness metadata.

tasks.name: Test suite & fixtures for CSV pipeline
tasks.details: Add unit tests for parsing/normalization rules plus integration tests that run the pipeline over committed sample fixtures and assert row counts and key outputs. Done when the suite runs in CI in under two minutes.

tasks.name: Inventory application log sources & formats
tasks.details: Collect representative app log samples and document formats (JSON vs. plain text), severity levels, rotation/retention, timestamp formats, and services emitting logs. Output a findings note plus anonymized fixtures.

tasks.name: Define log event schema & parsing spec
tasks.details: Specify the canonical log event record (timestamp, service, level, message, request ID, latency, status code, error class) and the extraction patterns (regex/grok or JSON paths) per log format. Done when every sample line type has a documented and testable pattern.

tasks.name: Build log ingestion & multi-line parser
tasks.details: Implement the log reader that handles multi-line entries (stack traces), malformed lines, and large files in a streaming fashion, writing structured events to the raw log table. Done when unparseable-line rate is reported and the parser handles a 1GB sample without loading it fully into memory.

tasks.name: Normalize & deduplicate log records
tasks.details: Convert timestamps to UTC, standardize severity/service/endpoint naming, enrich with environment and host metadata, and remove duplicate ingestion of the same line. Done when a re-run of the same file does not double-count events.

tasks.name: Compute reliability metrics
tasks.details: Aggregate error rate by service/hour, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), request volume, and failed-request counts into a metrics table. Done when values match an independently computed check on the sample data within tolerance.

tasks.name: Compute usage & error-trend metrics
tasks.details: Derive endpoint hit counts, top-N errors by frequency, active request traces, and daily/weekly trend series for dashboard consumption. Done when each metric is a queryable table with documented grain and time zone.

tasks.name: Build curated log aggregate tables & retention rules
tasks.details: Materialize hourly/daily aggregates and apply retention (e.g., raw logs 90 days, aggregates indefinite). Done when aggregates rebuild deterministically from raw and old partitions are purged by the retention job.

tasks.name: Test suite & fixtures for log pipeline
tasks.details: Test the parsing patterns against committed log fixtures (plain text, JSON, stack traces, malformed lines) and add integration checks on the aggregate tables. Done when parsing coverage is measured and CI runs the suite.

tasks.name: Dashboard UX & information architecture
tasks.details: Define the dashboard's pages, user journeys, and KPI hierarchy (customer health, acquisition trends, reliability). Produce low-fidelity wireframes and a metric-to-view map. Done when every curated table from M2/M3 has a defined home on a screen.

tasks.name: Set up design system & component library
tasks.details: Establish theme tokens (color, spacing, typography), base UI primitives (cards, tables, badges, loading/empty states), and a chart color palette that is colorblind-safe. Done when tokens are consumed from one source of truth.

tasks.name: Build app shell, routing & responsive layout
tasks.details: Create the front-end app shell: navigation, page routing, responsive grid, loading and error boundaries. Use mocked data for now. Done when the app builds, routes between placeholder pages, and works at desktop and tablet widths.

tasks.name: Build core chart primitives
tasks.details: Wrap the charting library into reusable primitives: line, bar, stacked bar, donut, histogram, and KPI stat card — each with tooltips, legends, empty states, and consistent formatting. Done when each primitive renders from a typed data prop and has a demo story/page.

tasks.name: Build customer analytics views
tasks.details: Compose the customer page: totals and KPI cards, segment breakdown, acquisition/cohort trend, and a searchable customer table. Wire to mocked-then-real curated data. Done when all customer metrics from M2 are visible and page loads under 2s on sample data.

tasks.name: Build log & reliability views
tasks.details: Compose the reliability page: error-rate timeline, latency percentile chart, request volume, and top-errors table with drill-down. Done when all reliability metrics from M3 are visible with correct labels and units.

tasks.name: Add global filters & cross-filtering
tasks.details: Implement a global filter bar (date range, segment, service, environment) with URL-persisted state and cross-filtering across charts. Done when selecting a filter updates all bound widgets and the state survives a page reload.

tasks.name: Accessibility & responsive polish
tasks.details: Add keyboard navigation, ARIA labels, chart text alternatives, and mobile breakpoints. Run an automated accessibility scan and fix reported issues. Done when scan shows no critical violations and pages are usable at 375px width.

tasks.name: Component tests & visual regression baseline
tasks.details: Add component tests for chart primitives and page containers, plus screenshot-based visual regression baselines for the main views. Done when CI fails on an unintended visual diff.

tasks.name: Define API contract between data layer & UI
tasks.details: Specify REST/GraphQL endpoints for customer metrics, segment rollups, reliability metrics, and filter parameters, with request/response examples and pagination rules. Done when the front-end can be built against a documented contract.

tasks.name: Build data access & query API layer
tasks.details: Implement the API service that reads curated tables, applies filters/time ranges, caches hot queries, and returns typed responses per the contract. Done when all endpoints respond correctly against sample data and have request-level logging.

tasks.name: Wire CSV pipeline through to the API
tasks.details: Connect the curated customer tables to their API endpoints and replace the front-end mock with real calls. Done when a CSV drop → pipeline run → dashboard refresh shows updated customer numbers.

tasks.name: Wire log pipeline through to the API
tasks.details: Connect curated log/metric tables to their API endpoints and switch reliability widgets to real data. Done when ingesting a new log file updates the reliability page after one pipeline run.

tasks.name: End-to-end dashboard integration pass
tasks.details: Join customer segments with reliability metrics where relevant, verify every widget against its source table, and resolve loading/empty/error states with real data. Done when a click-through of all pages shows no mock data and no console errors.

tasks.name: Performance & load testing on representative volumes
tasks.details: Benchmark pipeline run time and API/dashboard latency against realistic data volumes; profile slow queries and add indexes or pre-aggregation as needed. Done when p95 dashboard load is under an agreed target and results are documented.

tasks.name: Security & PII access review
tasks.details: Verify PII is masked in curated tables and never reaches the browser unmasked, secrets are out of source control, API access is authenticated, and dashboards respect role-based visibility. Done when a checklist review is signed off with no open high-severity findings.

tasks.name: End-to-end test suite & acceptance run
tasks.details: Write smoke/E2E tests covering ingest → transform → API → UI for both domains, and run an acceptance checklist against agreed success criteria. Done when the full suite passes from a clean environment.

tasks.name: Deployment pipeline & environment provisioning
tasks.details: Add build/deploy automation (container images and CI job), provision dev/staging environments, and configure scheduled pipeline runs. Done when a tagged commit deploys automatically to staging and the dashboard is reachable there.

tasks.name: Ops runbook, monitoring & handover docs
tasks.details: Document how to run/backfill each pipeline, alert on failed runs and data staleness, and write a short handover guide (architecture, data dictionary, known limits). Done when a teammate can operate the system from the docs alone.
